summary.text: 非 is an old graph whose early form has been interpreted as opposed wings or as two people back-to-back. Oracle-bone examples already use it as a negative, but the evidence does not show how that use arose from either proposed image.

formation.text: The graph is a disputed pictograph: one interpretation sees wings facing away, another sees two people back-to-back. The evidence does not settle the referent or establish an internal sound component. The selected Shang-style illustration is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image.

components.text: Treat the graph as one whole picture. It has been interpreted as opposed wings or as two people back-to-back; the evidence does not decide between these readings.

history.text: The received Shuowen explanation connects 非 with the lower wings of 飛 facing away and glosses it as opposition. This is an old interpretation, not proof of the original referent or of a dated path from that image to negation. Another proposal reads early forms as two people back-to-back and relates 非 to 北; the accounts remain unresolved.

Oracle-bone, bronze, bamboo-slip, and seal forms are reported, but their inventory does not establish a complete sequence of graphic changes. The selected Shang-style illustration is a modern vector redraw associated with a Xiaoxuetang record, not an artifact photograph.

uncertainties.text: The original referent remains unresolved: early forms have competing wing and human interpretations. The proposed relation to 北 is disputed, and the evidence does not settle whether 非 is related to 飛.

Oracle-bone examples already use 非 as a negative, but the evidence does not show whether negation developed from an earlier pictorial or opposition sense. A separate, disputed proposal treats spoken 非 as a fusion of 不 and 惟; it does not mean the graph is composed of those characters.
No phonetic component within 非’s graphic formation is established in the cited analyses, so no component-level sound comparison is available.

senses.text: Reported oracle-bone examples use 非 as a negative. Oracle-bone script is the earliest script class identified here, though the examples’ absolute dates are unresolved.

senses.period: Han-era dictionary explanation; earlier use unresolved
senses.text: The received Shuowen explanation gives 非 the sense ‘opposition’ and connects it with wings facing away. This does not establish opposition as an earlier lexical stage.

senses.gloss: fault or wrongness; judging something wrong
senses.period: bronze inscriptions reported; absolute date unresolved
senses.text: Reported bronze examples use 非 for faults and for judging something wrong. Their semantic or chronological relation to the negative use is unresolved.
Later dictionary records include uses meaning reproach or criticize, but do not establish their path from the negative sense.
A later dictionary records an ‘avoid’ sense; its relation to the other senses is unresolved.
Modern references give negative meanings including ‘not’ and ‘non-’.

limitations.text: Early negative attestations do not establish whether the negative sense developed from a pictorial meaning or from opposition; no dated transition is supplied.
Reported uses for wrongness, reproach, and avoidance do not establish a complete chronology or their connections to one another or to negation.
The proposed 不 + 惟 fusion is a disputed account of the spoken word 非. It does not show that the graph was formed from 不 and 惟 or identify the name of a depicted object.

overview.text: 非 is an old graph already used as a negative in oracle-bone inscriptions. Its early picture is disputed: it may show opposed wings or two people back-to-back, and the evidence does not show how either image led to ‘not’.

components.text: Read the whole graph as one disputed picture: opposed wings in one interpretation, or two people back-to-back in another. The evidence does not settle which.
